title: Cohortless batch-adapter diagnostics labbook
content:
Status: working labbook (notes + intermediate results)
Owner: Priya Nair; collaborators: Liam, Maya, Noah
Context:
- Goal: isolate why tail latency spikes persist in continuous-batching mode under mixed bursty and steady traffic despite earlier tuning. We suspect interactions between small-batch timeout choices and fairness heuristics create pathological starvation for some request cohorts.
- This doc collects profiling outputs, experiment matrix, microtrace patterns, and quick wins for immediate mitigation. Not a final write-up.

Key hypotheses:
1) Aggressive timeout reductions (10ms range) reduce p50 but increase p99 due to increased scheduling churn and kernel launch overhead on GPU for many tiny batches.
2) Fairness policies that demote by age-only cause starvation of late-arriving long-sequence requests (longer KV cache misses), amplifying tail latency.
3) Cohortless batch adapter (no explicit cohort isolation) can show improved average throughput but worse tail when workload mixes short and long sequences — metric: p99 tokens/service-second.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variables: batch_max_size ∈ {4, 8, 16}, timeout_ms ∈ {8, 15, 30, 60}, fairness_policy ∈ {none, age-weighted, size-aware}, cohort_adapter ∈ {enabled, disabled}
- Workloads: steady_low (5 qps per worker), bursty_micro (100 qps for 200ms spikes every 5s), mixed (steady background + occasional large arrival bursts), cold_kv (simulated KV cache miss rate 30%)
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (ms) per-request and per-token, batch_fill_ratio, batch_count/sec, GPU_util%, CPU sched delay (ms), kernel_launch_count, per-batch token throughput, aborted_preemption_count, request_age_distribution at dispatch

Instrumentation notes (how we profiled):
- Enabled microtrace (trace-id per request) in serving runtime; collected first-byte timestamps for queue_enter, queue_emit, batch_form, kernel_launch, kv_miss, kv_hit, kv_fetch_done, response_sent.
- Used eBPF-based sampling to measure sys-sched latency spikes on CPU when queue reordering occurs.
- GPU metrics via DCGM sampled at 200ms bucket; correlated with batch_kernel sizes.
- Added debug histogram counters for "demoted_by_fairness" and "demotion_depth" per-request.

Representative run notes (raw):
Run A: batch_max_size=4, timeout=8ms, fairness=none, cohort_adapter=disabled, workload=bursty_micro
- Observed: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=420ms. Batch_fill_ratio=0.38. kernel_launch_count high (+27% vs baseline). GPU_util=62%. Many tiny kernels (avg tokens per kernel=3.4).
- Microtrace pattern: multiple back-to-back kernel launches for same request (due to small batches + long seqs), queue_emit happening right when burst arrives, causing preemption.

Run B: batch_max_size=16, timeout=60ms, fairness=age-weighted, cohort_adapter=enabled, workload=mixed
- Observed: p50=68ms, p95=140ms, p99=260ms. Batch_fill_ratio=0.86. kernel_launch_count lower. GPU_util=87%. Long-sequence requests saw fewer demotions.
- Downside: steady-state cost per token increased slightly due to larger sequences held in queue longer.

Run C (diagnostic): batch_max_size=8, timeout=15ms, fairness=size-aware, cohort_adapter=disabled, workload=cold_kv
- Observed: p50=58ms, p95=190ms, p99=670ms. Significant KV fetch latency (avg kv_fetch_done delta +120ms) pushed several requests past timeout boundary and triggered requeuing. demoted_by_fairness counters low but starvation flags high.

Key profiling takeaways:
- Kernel launch overhead dominates when average batch tokens per kernel < ~6; payback from batching disappears. Use a conservative lower bound batch size to avoid tiny kernels.
- Timeout too low + no fairness => excessive churn: queues flush often with underfilled batches, more kernel launches, more context switches. Tail suffers.
- Fairness policies that only consider arrival age are blind to compute cost; size-aware heuristics reduce worst-case p99 for mixed-length workloads.
- Cohort-adapter (explicitly separating short vs long requests into different batch lanes) reduces tail significantly at modest cost in average latency. It is promising in production as an isolation knob.

Immediate mitigations to try (fast rollouts):
1) Set runtime default: min_batch_tokens threshold = 6 for models with small token-per-request distributions; fall back to timeout if not reached after 60ms.
2) Enable size-aware fairness in canary for Dedicated clusters with mixed workloads.
3) Add a soft backoff for requeueing requests that encountered KV miss to avoid immediate demotion cascades.
4) Instrument "kernel fragmentation" alert (when kernel_launch_count / batch_count > 1.5 over 30s).

Longer-term experiments / next steps:
- A/B test cohort-adapter lanes across 2 pods in Dedicated: measure p99 vs cost delta (expected p99 decrease 30–50% for mixed workloads). Track per-customer regressions. (JIRA:INF-7901)
- Explore adaptive timeout controller: reacts to incoming QPS and measured batch_fill_ratio; increases timeout during high burstiness to allow better coalescing, decreases timeout during steady low QPS for latency improvement.
- Microbench kernel-level: modify kernel merging strategy to reduce overhead of many tiny launches. Work with infra team on fused kernels prototype.

Open questions / unresolved smells:
- Observed a small set of requests that hit p99 repeatedly even when cohorts enabled — need to inspect model-level op patterns (attention refills?)
- Are there cross-request effects from KV prefetch that create a thundering herd on KV backend when fairness demotions requeue many long requests simultaneously?

Notes to reviewers:
- Data exported to /experiments/batching/2024-11/ has raw traces and the trace->event extractor notebook. See linked GitHub PR for debug flags used.
- Please review the proposed default change (min_batch_tokens=6, timeout_cap=60ms) in PR #1456 and weigh cost vs SLA trade-offs for small customers.

Appendix (quick run commands used):
- ./serving-runtime --experiment=batching_cohortless_diag --batch-max-size=8 --timeout-ms=15 --fairness=size-aware --trace-enabled=true --min-batch-tokens=0
- profiler: ./tools/collect-traces --trace-ids recent --out=./experiments/batching/2024-11/raw.tgz

Action items
- Priya: queue adaptive-timeout prototype spike (2 wks).
- Liam: extend demotion counters with per-model breakdown and surface in Console.
- Maya: run 72h A/B on Dedicated canary with cohort-adapter enabled; collect cost and p99 deltas.
- Noah: follow up with infra on fused kernel feasibility.

End of labbook entry (intermediate).
